faults.detail: The mix-up is 'a tilted square corner is not a right angle'. The first challenge lets the child build any square, so a child holding the mix-up can build a flat, axis-aligned square and pass without ever judging a tilted corner. Nothing asks the child to decide whether a tilted corner is a right angle.

faults.where: rounds[0].challenges[1] {"kind":"rigid","frame":[[2,1],[6,2],[5,6],[1,5]]}; strings.rigid "Brace lagao: hilna nahi chahiye"
faults.detail: The tilted frame is a tilted square, but the task is to brace it so it does not wobble (rigidity). That practises bracing, not recognising right angles (topic c4-maths-ch01-t02), and it never asks whether the tilted corners are right angles.
The round has 2 challenges (a square and a rigid frame), and one challenge, "Banao square", is on screen, but the counter shows a total of 0. The count disagrees with its own round.
An all-English feedback line in a Hinglish piece (lang "hinglish").
At 412 px the SAMAY pill runs past the right edge of the card. The pill is clipped, and the timer bar that shows at l1366 is not visible.

notes: Only the first screen is shown, so I could not see how the rigid-frame challenge is presented or graded on screen. At l1366 the UNDO/CHECK buttons sit right next to the last column of grid dots. They do not clearly overlap, so I did not count it.

faults.detail: The mix-up is "Thinks zero is neither odd nor even" (signs: leaves 0 out of even numbers, unsure whether 10 or 20 is even). Every round just draws random numbers from 0-70; nothing in the spec puts 0 (or 10, 20, ...) in front of the child, so a child holding the belief can play every round without the belief ever going wrong. The first screen shows "43", a plain odd number unrelated to zero. The rounds are labelled as targeting the mix-up but do not confront it.

faults.where: l1366 screen: rule pill "Daura 1 sam" and the falling "43" hexagon
faults.detail: At 1366 px the rule pill "Daura 1 sam" sits over the top of the "43" hexagon, so the token's outline is cut off by the pill. The number is still legible, but the two elements overlap on the first screen.

notes: Whether the seeded draws happen to include 0 or multiples of 10 cannot be seen in the packet. The fault rests on the spec having no way to make sure they appear. 'sam'/'visham' for even/odd are correct, and no other text gives the answer away.

faults.detail: The "SEAL" label under the dial overlaps the bottom border of the "Nishana / sixteen / jama 0" panel: the border line runs through the top of the letters, so the label and the panel edge collide.

notes: At both sizes the leftmost block on the conveyor above "Jagah ke blocks chuno" is clipped by the card's left edge. A still frame cannot show whether this is a belt scrolling in by design or real clipping, so it is not counted. The content is on the mix-up: "sixteen" (words) is followed by 60 (digits) with only T/O columns, so a child who believes teen = ty would load 6 tens and go over. 6007 and 7608 are correct for their denominations, and 7608 matches the topic card key.

faults.detail: The mix-up is lining up numbers of different lengths from the left (e.g. 48 under the 32 of 3256). The only round asks for change from ₹20 for ₹12.50 (2000 − 1250 if read as paise: both 4 digits). No number of a different length appears, so a child who misaligns is never caught. The screen also turns it into a decimal rupee-paise subtraction (₹20 − ₹12.50), not the 4-digit whole-number add/subtract of this topic.
The round has 1 customer, but the served counter shows a total of 0 ("0/0"), which disagrees with its own round. It should read 0/1.
Misspelt: the Hinglish for 'count' (गिनो) is "gino", not "ginno".

notes: The spec gives price 1250 and pays 2000 with no unit. The screen shows them as ₹12.50 and ₹20, so the engine reads them as paise. I could not tell from the packet whether that was intended. The change itself (₹7.50) is correct for the values shown.
